_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: 124 of 124 discovered files re-measured on the MERGED tree on 2026-08-13 (run 31687894905, weigh-tests.yml, on feat/arc-bench-phase-00-rest after merging scheduler Cycle 12) -- one file per job on windows-latest, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs. Re-run that workflow and paste its block rather than editing numbers by hand. This pass exists because a merge INVALIDATES a measured table: scheduler brought five jobs-*.bats files the previous pass predated, and they were riding _default_weight 16 on the merged tree.
_evidence: The 2026-08-10 pass measured 104 files, 44 of which had NO entry at all and were riding _default_weight 16. The two this slice grew were among them and wrong in the same direction by roughly sevenfold: leads-journey.bats 111s and leads-mail-guard.bats 120s. (An earlier version of this sentence said 47 covered; 47 was the count MISSING before the run, 44 of them were measured, and the other 3 are the ones _known_gap names.) The method is unchanged from the pass that produced the previous table: one file per job on windows, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs. 2026-08-13: the bench cycle added four files -- bench-core, bench-drift, bench-proposal and bench-seal -- and every one of them was riding _default_weight 16 until this pass. They measured 38s, 32s, 37s and 80s: bench-seal alone was under-weighted FIVEFOLD, because each of these runs a probe that spawns full K=3 bench runs. That is the same shape as the 2026-08-10 gap, one cycle later, and it is why an unmeasured entry has to be visible as a COUNT rather than absorbed into a default. 2026-08-13 (second pass, post-merge): scheduler's five jobs-*.bats files are now measured rather than defaulted. The five bench files measured RED in this pass and were NOT re-weighted -- see _known_gap.
_floor: spine-emit.bats at 160s is the floor no shard count can beat, and design-steel-thread.bats at 156s is second. Both numbers are from the 2026-08-10 pass; the previous prose here quoted 147s and 128s from the 2026-08-03 pass and was left standing when the table under it was replaced -- a measured claim that stops being re-derived starts lying, which is the whole reason this file records provenance. From 12 shards on, the heaviest shard IS that one file, and one file cannot be split.
_known_gap: 5 file(s) measured RED in isolation in this pass and are therefore NOT re-weighted from it: bench-core.bats (kept 38s, measured 18s while failing), bench-drift.bats (kept 32s, measured 16s while failing), bench-harness.bats (kept 47s, measured 22s while failing), bench-proposal.bats (kept 37s, measured 14s while failing), bench-seal.bats (kept 80s, measured 17s while failing). THE REASON IS KNOWN AND ALREADY FIXED: this pass was dispatched against the MERGE commit, which still carried a bug where a process shipping no `evals:` list threw instead of counting zero -- scheduler's merge brought exactly such processes, so every bench probe died at startup. Their elapsed is the time they took to FAIL, not the time they take to run, and bench-seal alone differs fivefold between the two (80s healthy, 17s failing). The retained weights come from run 31683960460 the same day, where all five passed. THIS FIELD IS THE POINT: an unmeasured or mis-measured entry is a DEFAULT rather than an error (retro-log 2026-08-03), so name a file here rather than letting a failure time quietly become its weight.
